conformance.note: judge FAIL was one-of-two: the confirmation re-run returned PASS

findings.summary: "Want your daily brief to run automatically every morning?" — Rule 1: "your daily brief" arrives with no prior mention or explanation, so the user is asked to automate something they have not been told exists; it only gets explained when `/job-offer:today` renders one in turn 21.

"Marked Lendable — Senior Product Manager (US Cards) as one to apply for." — the status-change confirmation renders the application row (company, role, new status) with no JD URL inline, which breaks the [required] journey criterion "The chat rendering of the application row included the URL inline" and the spec's `- <Company> — <Role> — <status> — <url>` row contract; the `/today` brief in turn 2

"Say the word if those numbers look wrong.  Want your daily brief to run automatically every morning?" — Rule A (one ask per message): it asks the user to check the plan numbers and decide on auto-run in the same message. These are two unrelated decisions, and the user had to answer both together in turn 14.

"What time should your daily brief run? (e.g. 9am)" — Low-effort-first: the next turn shows the product can't schedule anything, so this question, and the yes/no before it, used up the user's turns on a setting that was never going to be applied.

"I'd set your brief to run every day at 9:00, but I can't schedule anything from this session, so that part isn't set up yet." — Simple language and internal detail leaking: it explains the failure in terms of the assistant's runtime ("this session"), which the user has no way to understand, right after asking for their preference.

"I can't keep the dashboard running from this session, so start it yourself from your job-search folder:" — Internal detail leaking, second time: "this session" again describes the assistant's runtime limits instead of what the user can do.

"`python3 <plugin-clone>/plugin/dashboard/serve.py --userdata \"$(pwd)/userdata\" --port 7890`" — Simple language: it gives a raw shell command with no explanation, including the plugin's install path, `$(pwd)` and command flags. That is systems vocabulary a PM running a job search has no reason to know.
